summary: The study investigates the enhancement of photoluminescence (PL) intensity from Si nanodots using Al2O3 surface passivation layers grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The ALD process uses trimethylaluminum (TMA) and water vapor as precursors at 300 ◦C. The Al2O3 passivation layer significantly reduces non-radiative recombination, thereby enhancing PL intensity over a wide temperature range. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of ALD-grown Al2O3 layers for surface passivation in nanostructured silicon devices.
